notes: The prompt stated "Source follows" but no source lines were actually included, so no file:line citations could be produced; every tool is marked undetermined and evidence points at the advertised tool descriptors that were supplied.

All 24 tools are thin OpenAPI-proxy operations over api.notion.com authenticated with a single operator-configured Notion token (typically NOTION_TOKEN / OPENAPI_MCP_HEADERS in this package). Because the endpoint host is fixed by the spec and not agent-chosen, write operations are not treated as SINKs; if the shipped code lets a caller override the base URL or headers per request, the write tools would become SINKs — this could not be checked without the source.

Notion content read back by the read tools is data in the user's own account, so UNTRUSTED was not raised for page/block/database reads. API-retrieve-a-comment is the exception: comment threads are a multi-writer surface (guests, external collaborators, other integrations) and are returned verbatim.

Potential secondary channels that could not be inspected without source: `cover`/`icon` external URLs on API-patch-page and API-post-page (fetched by Notion's servers), and `link` targets inside richTextRequest. These were not counted as SINKs.

No tool in the advertised set fetches an arbitrary user-supplied URL or executes code, so no HOSTEXEC label was assigned; a general "fetch"/URL tool present in some Notion MCP builds is absent from this list.
No flag- or toolset-gated tools were identifiable from the advertised list, so default_enabled is true for all; this could change if the source gates tools behind an env var or toolset selection.
